guarantees.claim: err_vld is the logical OR of op_update_i and op_done_i.
When err_vld is high, sync_err_d[SyncErrInvalidOp] is set to the OR of invalid_op_i, disabled_i, invalid_i, and the reduction-OR of fault_o.
When err_vld is high, sync_err_d[SyncErrInvalidIn] equals kmac_input_invalid_i.

assumptions.claim: The indices SyncErrInvalidOp and SyncErrInvalidIn are within the range [0, SyncErrLastIdx-1] as defined by keymgr_pkg.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds bit selection on sync_err_d, leading to undefined behavior or simulation error.

assumptions.claim: The inputs invalid_op_i, disabled_i, invalid_i, and fault_o must be stable while err_vld (op_update_i | op_done_i) is high.
assumptions.risk: Glitches on sync_err_d may be captured by the downstream register, causing spurious or missed error latching.

uncertain_points.claim: The logic that generates fault_o and the connection from sync_err_d to sync_err_o is not shown in this chunk; missing or incorrect logic could prevent sync_err_o from reflecting captured errors.
uncertain_points.cond: any error condition requiring output propagation
uncertain_points.risk: sync_err_o may be stuck at 0 or incorrectly driven, causing error detection failures downstream.
